support.title: Prevent and treat nausea
support.text: Ceritinib has moderate-to-high oral sickness risk. Ask for daily prevention and rescue instructions. Your team must check heart-rhythm and medicine interactions when choosing anti-sickness treatment; do not add medicines or a steroid course yourself.

support.title: Food and daily doses
support.text: If illness prevents you eating with the dose, contact the team. Only the prescriber can arrange a different fasting dose. Do not alternate between fed and fasting schedules or change the dose yourself.

support.title: Check interactions
support.text: Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice and St John’s wort. Check prescription, pharmacy and herbal medicines before use, including heart medicines, antibiotics, antifungals, seizure treatments and acid-reducing medicines. Do not stop a prescribed medicine without advice.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and feeding
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months afterwards; hormonal contraception may be less effective, so agree a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during this treatment. Fertility effects are uncertain; ask about preservation if relevant.

support.title: Diarrhoea, fluids and daily life
support.text: Use the agreed diarrhoea treatment promptly. Report persistent symptoms, poor intake or dehydration. Ask for help with appetite, fatigue and practical support; avoid driving or machinery if fatigue or visual symptoms affect safety.

evidence.title: Evidence after crizotinib and for dosing with food
evidence.intro: Study results describe groups, not an individual forecast.
evidence.population: Advanced ALK-positive NSCLC; post-crizotinib/platinum ASCEND-5 and separate dose-optimisation ASCEND-8 populations.
evidence.comparison_label: Historical chemotherapy or alternative food/dose schedules
evidence.interpretation: A study after crizotinib and platinum chemotherapy found longer disease control with ceritinib than the chemotherapy used at that time. It tested an older fasting dose. A separate dose study supports taking the current lower dose with food; its main efficacy group had not had previous treatment. These studies cannot predict your outcome or rank all current treatment options.
evidence.limitations: Trials used different doses and populations. No proven individual benefit or cross-trial ranking is implied.

patient.administration_text: Take at the same time daily with food. Swallow capsules whole with water; do not chew or crush. Take a missed dose unless the next is due within 12 hours; ask your pharmacist if timing is unclear. Never double a dose. If you vomit, do not replace the dose; take the next at its usual time. If illness prevents you eating with the dose, contact the team. Only the prescriber can arrange a different fasting dose. Do not alternate between fed and fasting schedules or change the dose yourself.

Extra heart, electrolyte, glucose or pancreatic tests may be needed for risks, symptoms or abnormal results; scans follow the consultant plan.

clinical.component_rationale: Ceritinib inhibits ALK signalling in a tumour with a confirmed ALK rearrangement. It can affect healthy tissues too, so blood tests and symptom checks continue even when treatment is taken at home.
key_points: The usual starting dose is 450 mg once daily with food, every day without a planned rest week. Follow your own prescription. Treatment continues while it helps and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed course length.

Adults with ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with crizotinib: NCCP 00340a. This suite does not turn the broader first-line licence into an NCCP indication or funding approval. Confirm your treatment setting with the team.
Any treatment-related ILD: permanently stop; suspected ILD alone requires investigation, not irreversible attribution.
ALT/AST >3 ×ULN plus bilirubin >2 ×ULN requires absence of cholestasis/haemolysis before permanent stop.
QT source thresholds use strictly >500 ms or >60 ms rise with arrhythmia; repeated ECG context must be distinguished.
Moderate-high oral emetic risk; tailored prophylaxis after QT/interaction review.

NCCP v4 p2 excludes moderate or severe hepatic impairment, while p3 Table 2 permits Child–Pugh A/B without adjustment and C at 67% of original dose. Current EMA SmPC also permits moderate impairment and a one-third reduction for severe impairment. This internal NCCP conflict requires Consultant/pharmacy resolution; no automatic hepatic dose is calculated.

NCCP v4 p3 expects no renal adjustment even below CrCl 30 mL/min or on haemodialysis. EMA SmPC 4.2 cautions that severe impairment has no clinical experience; severe renal impairment/dialysis require individual specialist review.
NCCP 00340a is post-crizotinib ALK-positive advanced NSCLC. The EMA licence also includes first-line disease; that does not expand this NCCP suite or establish reimbursement.

The standard current schedule is 450 mg once daily with food. Historical 750 mg fasting trial results cannot be presented as trials of the current fed schedule. Only a clinician-directed inability-to-eat switch uses the specific alternate schedule; patients must not alternate fed and fasted dosing.

NCCP v4 Table 3 does not specify a CTCAE edition. Preserve clinically confirmed grades without labelling them CTCAE v5. The source glucose threshold is strictly >250 mg/dL, not a rounded 13.9 mmol/L threshold.

rationale.summary: Ceritinib blocks abnormal ALK signals that help some lung cancers grow. In advanced cancer after crizotinib, the aim is to control cancer and delay progression. The choice depends on your tumour test, previous treatment, other options and priorities.
factors: Validated ALK result and prior crizotinib
CNS disease, prior treatment sequence, organ/cardiac status, interactions and patient priorities
Current MDT options and actual access
alternatives: Discuss suitable molecular therapies, systemic treatment, clinical trials and supportive care, including not proceeding.
limitations: Adults with ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with crizotinib: NCCP 00340a. This suite does not turn the broader first-line licence into an NCCP indication or funding approval. Confirm your treatment setting with the team.
ASCEND-5 enrolled patients after both platinum chemotherapy and crizotinib, not every modern ALK inhibitor sequence. It used ceritinib 750 mg fasting; the current NCCP regimen is 450 mg with food.
ASCEND-5 primary PFS analysis had median follow-up 16.5 months; OS at that analysis was immature/confounded by crossover and did not establish an OS advantage.

ASCEND-8 was an open-label phase I dose/food optimisation study; primary efficacy analysis included 198 treatment-naive ALK-IHC-positive participants. Its response rates are not a post-crizotinib outcome estimate or proof of equivalence.
No cross-trial ranking of contemporary ALK therapies or individual survival prediction.
Independent consultant, pharmacy and patient/PPI review remains pending.

evidence.population: ASCEND-5: 231 adults with advanced ALK-positive NSCLC after crizotinib and one or two chemotherapy lines including platinum. ASCEND-8: mixed prior-treatment safety/PK population; treatment-naive ALK-IHC-positive efficacy subset.
evidence.comparison: ASCEND-5: ceritinib 750 mg fasting versus pemetrexed or docetaxel. ASCEND-8: 450 mg with food, 600 mg with food or 750 mg fasting.
evidence.applicability: Post-crizotinib indication evidence and current fed-dose rationale are separate; not a first-line NCCP expansion.

endpoints.interpretation: Primary 2017 analysis; median follow-up 16.5 months, 231 randomised. HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.36–0.67), p<0.0001. Prior platinum and crizotinib; historical comparator and fasting dose. This is not an OS gain.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published study-population result; not an individual prediction

endpoints.interpretation: Primary 2019 efficacy analysis, 27 March 2018 cutoff: treatment-naive ALK-IHC-positive subset, median follow-up 14.3 months. 95% CIs 66.9–86.9 and 64.3–84.9. Dose-optimisation study, not powered proof of equivalence and not a post-crizotinib response estimate.
endpoints.analysis_status: Secondary efficacy endpoint in phase I dose optimisation; population mismatch explicit

limitations: Adults with ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with crizotinib: NCCP 00340a. This suite does not turn the broader first-line licence into an NCCP indication or funding approval. Confirm your treatment setting with the team.
ASCEND-5 enrolled patients after both platinum chemotherapy and crizotinib, not every modern ALK inhibitor sequence. It used ceritinib 750 mg fasting; the current NCCP regimen is 450 mg with food.
ASCEND-5 primary PFS analysis had median follow-up 16.5 months; OS at that analysis was immature/confounded by crossover and did not establish an OS advantage.

ASCEND-8 was an open-label phase I dose/food optimisation study; primary efficacy analysis included 198 treatment-naive ALK-IHC-positive participants. Its response rates are not a post-crizotinib outcome estimate or proof of equivalence.
No cross-trial ranking of contemporary ALK therapies or individual survival prediction.
Independent consultant, pharmacy and patient/PPI review remains pending.
evidence.harms: GI toxicity and liver enzyme abnormalities were prominent. Current SmPC also describes serious hepatic, lung, cardiac, glucose and pancreatic risks. Frequencies from fasting historical trials are not transferred to the fed regimen.

medicines.note: NCCP V6 Table 5 supports daily oral 5-HT3 antagonist prophylaxis for moderate-high risk. Ceritinib can prolong QT and cause bradycardia; check ECG/electrolytes and interactions before selecting an agent. Do not copy an infusion steroid/NK1 bundle.

additional_support: Ceritinib has moderate-to-high oral sickness risk. Ask for daily prevention and rescue instructions. Your team must check heart-rhythm and medicine interactions when choosing anti-sickness treatment; do not add medicines or a steroid course yourself.

If illness prevents you eating with the dose, contact the team. Only the prescriber can arrange a different fasting dose. Do not alternate between fed and fasting schedules or change the dose yourself.

Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice and St John’s wort. Check prescription, pharmacy and herbal medicines before use, including heart medicines, antibiotics, antifungals, seizure treatments and acid-reducing medicines. Do not stop a prescribed medicine without advice.

Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months afterwards; hormonal contraception may be less effective, so agree a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during this treatment. Fertility effects are uncertain; ask about preservation if relevant.

Use the agreed diarrhoea treatment promptly. Report persistent symptoms, poor intake or dehydration. Ask for help with appetite, fatigue and practical support; avoid driving or machinery if fatigue or visual symptoms affect safety.
